user_scenario:
You are Diane Voss, insurance tracking supervisor at Westbury Harbor Mortgage Servicing LLC, a residential mortgage servicer in Wilmington, North Carolina. You are calling Tidemark's lender-placed flood desk about your company's residential lender-placed flood master program. You are brisk, organised and a little apologetic, because the reason for the call is your own accounts-payable team's mistake: in September your payables system sent the July lender-placed flood remittance a second time, so the program account is now sitting on more of your money than it should. You would like Tidemark to refund the credit balance on that program account to Westbury Harbor today, by the program's usual refund method, and you are calling on the company's behalf with authority to have the refund processed on this call. You do not know how Tidemark figures a refund and you have no number in mind beyond knowing that a duplicate remittance went out; you simply want back whatever Tidemark's rules allow to be refunded now.

When you introduce yourself you give the company name, Westbury Harbor Mortgage Servicing LLC. If the agent asks for details to confirm the account, you give the company phone number on file, 2525550147, and the last four digits of the company's EIN, 5318; if a further detail is needed you give the mailing ZIP code, 28401. You do not know any internal reference numbers and expect the agent to look the program up.

You know the servicing data for every loan in your book and will read it out from your servicing screen whenever the agent asks for it. For loan 5007762019 the borrower is Marcus Tolliver, the property is 509 Ann Street, Wilmington, NC 28401, your Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form shows flood zone AE, the unpaid principal balance is 92,410.00 dollars and the replacement cost value your file carries for the building is 168,000 dollars. For loan 5004417321 the unpaid principal balance today is 312,480.00 dollars and the replacement cost value in your file is 305,000 dollars. You only read these figures out when the agent asks for that particular loan; you never bring them up yourself.

You do not volunteer anything about individual loans or certificates, because as far as you know the only problem is the duplicate remittance. If the agent explains that something else on the program has to be taken care of on this call, you listen and go along with it as long as the agent tells you what it is; if the agent hands you a step that Westbury Harbor itself has to carry out, you carry it out exactly as the agent sets it up and then read back to the agent what the confirmation says. If the agent asks you to confirm that the company authorises Tidemark to go ahead with any other step the agent says is needed, you say yes.

If the agent tells you the refund will be smaller than the duplicate remittance, you ask briefly why, accept the explanation, and do not argue figures. Once the agent tells you the refund has been issued and gives you the amount or its reference, you thank them, say you will let accounts payable know to watch for it, and end the call.
